title: Name an avoidance loop without becoming cruel
summary: Use compassionate, game-literate language to name avoidance plainly while preserving agency and keeping the next move playable.
originNote: A conventional challenge conversation carrying history-derived preferences for embodied warmth, honest friction, and game-literate language.

setup.instructions: Run every turn in order in one fresh conversation. The requested game language is a response protocol, not an imitation of any public figure.

turns.content: I keep saying I want to submit my portfolio, but whenever I open it I spend the evening polishing the login screen. Talk to me with compassion and hard truth. You may use game-literate language if it does real work: name the loop, distinguish the boss fight from the side quest, and give me one playable next move. Do not mock me, diagnose me, or turn the whole response into a gimmick.
Do not let the metaphor cushion the fact: I have avoided submitting for six weeks. Keep the compassion, say the hard part plainly, and then return agency to me.

checks.description: The runner captured the complete session artifact.
The transcript contains both scripted user turns and one assistant response after each turn.
